title: K-flat open tensor map computes the derived coefficient projection
statement:
Let $j:U\hookrightarrow P$ be an open immersion of schemes and let $A\to B$ be a unital map of finite commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Use ordinary small etale module derived categories and localization $\ell$ from integer cochain complexes [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Write $T_W=-\otimes_A^LB_W$ and $\operatorname{Res}_W$ for exact restriction of scalars [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction]. Fix $L\in D(P_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ such that $L$, $Rj_{*,A}j^*L$, $T_PL$, $T_PRj_{*,A}j^*L$ and $Rj_{*,B}j^*T_PL$ are bounded below.

Choose a complex $I$ with $\ell I\simeq L$, a flat-term K-flat quasi-isomorphism $Q\to B_P[0]$ [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], and an $A$-linear quasi-isomorphism $a:N=\operatorname{Tot}(Q\otimes_A I)\to J$, where total tensor is [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Assume the canonical right-derived comparison maps for $j^*I$ and $j^*J$ are invertible:
$$\ell(j_*j^*I)\xrightarrow{\sim}Rj_{*,A}j^*(\ell I),\qquad\ell(j_*j^*J)\xrightarrow{\sim}Rj_{*,A}j^*(\ell J).$$
These are the canonical comparisons of [lem-sp-etale-derived-chain-transpose], not arbitrarily chosen isomorphisms. Set $C=j_*j^*I$, $C'=j_*j^*J$. With the ordinary counit $\varepsilon^0$ of $j^*\dashv j_*$ and the canonical cochain tensor comparison $c$ [lem-pur-cochain-pullback-tensor-coherence], let $v:Q\otimes C\to C'$ be the ordinary adjunct of
$$h=j^*a\,c_{Q,I}^{-1}(1\otimes\varepsilon^0_{j^*I})c_{Q,C}.$$

The flat-term K-flat tensor comparison, signed symmetry putting $B$ second, augmentation and normalized scalar/tensor isomorphism give a canonical isomorphism $e_N:\ell N\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Res}_P(T_PL)$ [lem-weil-pbc-kflat-fixed-tensor-triangulated, lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Set $e_J=e_N(\ell a)^{-1}$. The same tensor comparison applied to $C$ and the canonical direct-image computations give isomorphisms
$$\sigma:\ell(Q\otimes C)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Res}_P(T_PRj_{*,A}j^*L),\qquad\tau:\ell C'\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Res}_P(Rj_{*,B}j^*T_PL),$$
where the target uses $e_J$ and the canonical bounded-below direct-image/restriction and inverse-image/restriction comparisons [lem-sbc-canonical-restrict-scalars-functor-comparisons]. Under these specified identifications,
$$\tau\,\ell(v)=\operatorname{Res}_P(\beta_{j^*L})\,\sigma,$$
where $\beta_{j^*L}:T_PRj_{*,A}j^*L\to Rj_{*,B}T_Uj^*L\simeq Rj_{*,B}j^*T_PL$ is the coefficient projection defined as the scalar mate of the derived counit [lem-pur-etale-scalar-mate-projection]. More precisely, before the scalar comparisons, the derived transpose of $\ell(v)$ is
$$(\varepsilon_{j,j^*L}\otimes^L1_{B_U})\,c^{\mathrm{der}}_{Rj_*j^*L,B_P},$$
so $\ell(v)$ is exactly the canonical projection-formula morphism $\mathrm{PF}_j(j^*L,B_P)$ [def-kun-projection-formula-map]. The equalities are natural on the stated domain with these representing identifications. No strict $B$-module structure on $Q,I,J$ and no preservation of injectives by restriction of scalars is assumed.

proof.text: Write $b:Q\to B_P[0]$ for the augmentation and $d_X:\ell(Q\otimes X)\cong(\ell X)\otimes_A^LB_P$ for the fixed-factor tensor identification, with $B$ placed second. The fixed-K-flat tensor lemma applies to every complex $X$, not just K-flat $X$. Its naturality identifies $\ell(1_Q\otimes t)$ with $(\ell t)\otimes^L1_B$. To check the normalization against scalar extension, choose a flat-term K-flat resolution $R\to X$. The maps $Q\otimes R\to Q\otimes X$ and $Q\otimes R\to B_P\otimes R$ are quasi-isomorphisms, by K-flatness of $Q$ and $R$, respectively. On $R$, scalar extension is represented by $R\otimes B_P$, and the ordinary restricted scalar extension is the sheaf tensor product. Thus augmentation and signed symmetry give the stated $e_N$; doing this for $C$ and composing with the assumed canonical comparison $\alpha_I:\ell C\cong Rj_*j^*L$ gives $\sigma$. The construction on the common resolution is natural, so these identifications use the specified augmentation and not an arbitrary isomorphism.

Under $d_X$, localization of $c_{Q,X}:j^*(Q\otimes X)\cong j^*Q\otimes j^*X$ is the canonical derived tensor/pullback comparison, with the corresponding signed interchange of the factors. Here is the representative check also when $X$ is not K-flat. Choose $R\to X$ as in Step 1. Pullback preserves flat-term K-flat complexes, so $j^*Q$ and $j^*R$ are valid tensor representatives. On $(Q,R)$ the representative square defining the derived tensor/pullback isomorphism is exactly the localization of the ordinary comparison $c_{Q,R}$. Naturality of $c$ gives its commuting square for $R\to X$; the two tensor maps across that square are invertible after localization because $Q$ and $j^*Q$ are K-flat. Cancel these maps. This proves the same representative square for $(Q,X)$. Compatibility with $b:Q\to B_P[0]$ and the signed symmetry follows from naturality and the signed-symmetry equation for $c$. The representative-descent lemma ensures that this is the specified canonical derived comparison.

source.place: Tag 07A4, label lemma-pullback-tensor-product, proof on K-flat representatives

proof.text: Let $\alpha_J:\ell C'\to Rj_*\ell(j^*J)$ be the canonical comparison, assumed invertible. Apply the chain-transpose lemma with $M=Q\otimes C$, $K=j^*J$, and $f=v$. Since $v$ was defined as the ordinary adjunct of $h$, the derived transpose of $\alpha_J\ell(v)$ is precisely $\ell(h)$. Also the same lemma with $K=j^*I$ and $f=1_C$ gives the concrete counit equation $\varepsilon_{j,j^*L}\,j^*(\alpha_I)=\ell(\varepsilon^0_{j^*I})$, with the representing identification $\ell I\cong L$ understood. Both assertions apply to arbitrary complexes; neither uses injectivity or an acyclicity claim beyond the comparison isomorphisms explicitly assumed in the item.

source.place: Tag 0FPI, label lemma-adjoints-push-pull-compatibility, canonical counit square

proof.text:
Undo the target replacement by $j^*(\ell a)^{-1}$ and then identify $\ell N$ with $\operatorname{Res}_P(T_PL)$ using $e_N$. In the transpose, the initial factor $j^*\ell(a)$ in $\ell(h)$ cancels with $j^*(\ell a)^{-1}$. The remaining expression, in $Q$-first coordinates, is
$$\ell(c_{Q,I}^{-1})\,\ell(1_Q\otimes\varepsilon^0_{j^*I})\,\ell(c_{Q,C}).$$
Step 2 identifies the first and last factors with the tensor/pullback comparisons. Step 1 identifies the middle factor with tensoring the ordinary counit by $B$. Step 3 identifies that ordinary counit, after $\alpha_I$, with the derived counit. Moving $B$ second uses the same signed symmetry on both source and target; its compatibility with $c$ removes any extra sign. Consequently the normalized derived transpose is exactly
$$(\varepsilon_{j,j^*L}\otimes^L1_{B_U})c^{\mathrm{der}}_{Rj_*j^*L,B_P}.$$
This calculation also explains why the target uses $e_J=e_N(\ell a)^{-1}$ rather than an independently chosen identification.

source.place: Tags 0FPI and 07A4, tensoring the canonical counit square

proof.text: By the definition of the projection-formula morphism, the expression in Step 4 is the transpose defining $\mathrm{PF}_j(j^*L,B_P[0])$. The derived adjunction is a bijection on Hom sets, so equality of these transposes implies equality of the morphisms. Explicitly the target identification before changing coefficients is $Rj_*(j^*e_J)\alpha_J$; the source identification is $\sigma$ followed by the scalar/tensor identification. Thus the localization of the specified map $v$ is the canonical projection-formula morphism under precisely the identifications in the statement.

source.place: Tag 0FPI, canonical derived adjunct; projection formula defined by its transpose

proof.text: Apply the scalar-mate projection lemma with $f=j$ and its object $J=j^*L$. Its three bounded-below hypotheses hold: $j^*L$ and $T_Uj^*L=j^*T_PL$ are bounded below since exact pullback is termwise, while $T_PRj_{*,A}j^*L$ is bounded below by assumption. The additional assumed bound on $Rj_{*,B}j^*T_PL$ puts the direct-image/restriction comparison on its stated bounded-below domain. That lemma identifies this very projection-formula map with $\operatorname{Res}_P(\beta_{j^*L})$. The canonical direct-image and inverse-image/restriction comparisons identify $Rj_*(j^*e_J)\alpha_J$ with the stated $\tau$. Combining with Step 5 proves $\tau\ell(v)=\operatorname{Res}_P(\beta_{j^*L})\sigma$. All equations used above are natural in chain maps and in the localized tensor variables, and adjunction transposition is natural; hence the equality is natural whenever the specified representing identifications are used. No step equips $J$ with a strict $B$-action or asserts that restriction preserves injectives.

All six steps check against the exact statements of the 13 cited nodes. Step 1: the fixed-factor tensor lemma applies to every complex X; on a flat-term K-flat resolution R→X, Q⊗R→Q⊗X is a quasi-isomorphism because Q is K-flat and Q⊗R→B⊗R because R is; derived change of rings plus the change-of-rings tensor comparison then give e_N. Step 2: pullback preserves K-flatness with no flatness of A→B, and the cancellation argument is valid. Step 3: the chain-transpose lemma gives f^♭=h for f=v and the counit equation for f=1. Step 4: the three factors assemble to α_{E,K} with E=j^*L, K=B_P, with no stray sign. Step 5: def-kun-projection-formula-map defines PF as the adjoint of α_{E,K}, so equal transposes give equal maps. Step 6: the scalar-mate lemma's three bounded-below hypotheses hold through exact j^* and the assumed bounds, and its U(β)=PF conclusion with the bounded-below restriction comparisons gives τℓ(v)=Res(β)σ. Edge cases checked: j=id, U empty, A=B, and Z/4→Z/2 (no flatness of the coefficient map needed). Stacks 0FPI, 07A4 and 06YS labels confirmed in tags/tags, and 0FPI read. No cycle, no SGA, no duplicate node. I accept the 13 declared tool_uses as generic black-box uses; 3 are outside the unit route: lem-sp-etale-derived-chain-transpose, lem-sbc-canonical-restrict-scalars-functor-comparisons, and the definition def-kun-projection-formula-map. Maintainer notes: (a) Step 2 uses the fact that the canonical comparison of lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback is the localized ordinary comparison on K-flat pairs. That comes from the node's construction (proof step 5), not its statement; the cited descent-representatives uniqueness pins it, and lem-kun-inverse-image-monoidal's proof relies on the same fact. It would be cleaner stated in that node's statement. (b) Step 6's compatibility of Res(j^*T_P≅T_Uj^*) with c^der holds by the scalar-mate lemma's construction. (c) coord/dag-sync.md is absent from the snapshot. No fixes.
